disclaimer: This repository contains curated extracts of selected commercial provisions from Indian central statutes for lawyer-in-the-loop review. It does not constitute complete statutory Acts, official legal publications, or an exhaustive search of Indian law. Independent advocate verification of applicability, amendment status, and official gazette text is mandatory.

official_sources.title: The Information Technology Act, 2000
official_sources.issuing_authority: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology / Ministry of Law and Justice
official_sources.publisher: Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology / Ministry of Law and Justice
official_sources.source_scope: Curated electronic commerce, contract validity, and cyber liability provisions (extract)
official_sources.verification_notes: Local SHA-256 integrity verified; reference artifact acquired (SHA-256: 14e752718c878096...); 4/6 sections match official enactment; 2 sections contain researcher editorial notes; curated extract (6 of 94 sections).
official_sources.applicability_limitations: Curated extract. Section 66A struck down as unconstitutional (Shreya Singhal v. Union of India). Section 43A pending repeal upon full commencement of DPDP Act 2023 Section 44. Does not cover intermediary guidelines or CERT-In regulations.
official_sources.reviewer_notes: Section 66A flagged unconstitutional; Sec 43A transition noted.
extraction_warnings: Section 66A struck down as unconstitutional by Supreme Court of India in Shreya Singhal v. Union of India (2015) 5 SCC 1.
Section 43A subject to omission upon full commencement of Section 44 of Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023.
official_sources.notes: Governs electronic contracts (Sec 10A) and data breach liability (Sec 43A, 72A).

official_sources.title: The Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023
official_sources.issuing_authority: The Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs / Ministry of Law and Justice
official_sources.publisher: The Gazette of India, Ministry of Home Affairs / Ministry of Law and Justice
official_sources.verification_notes: Local SHA-256 integrity verified; reference artifact acquired (SHA-256: 760344a1f4b40aba...); 2/3 sections match official gazette; Section 1 contains researcher commencement note; curated extract (3 of 170 sections).
official_sources.applicability_limitations: Extract covers electronic records admissibility (Sec 61) and electronic record certificates (Sec 63). Does not cover other evidence provisions (oral, documentary, burden of proof, witnesses). Supersedes Indian Evidence Act 1872 for proceedings post-July 1, 2024.
official_sources.reviewer_notes: Commencement on 2024-07-01 verified via MHA notification S.O. 849(E).
extraction_warnings: Commenced on 1st July, 2024 vide Ministry of Home Affairs Notification S.O. 849(E). Supersedes the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
official_sources.notes: Governs admissibility of electronic records in commercial disputes (Sections 61 and 63).
